title: Bisection Algorithm: bisectStep, bisect, bisectMid
content: Three noncomputable definitions encode the bisection algorithm. bisectStep takes a pair (left, right) and a function f, computes mid = (left+right)/2, and keeps [mid, right] if f(mid) ≤ 0, otherwise keeps [left, mid]. bisect iterates this n times via structural recursion. bisectMid extracts the midpoint of the n-th iterate. All are noncomputable because they depend on real-valued function evaluation, which is generally undecidable.
mathContext: $\text{bisectStep}(f, (l, r)) = \begin{cases} ((l+r)/2, r) & \text{if } f((l+r)/2) \leq 0 \\ (l, (l+r)/2) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$. Iterating $n$ times gives $\text{bisect}(f, n, (a,b))$.

title: Width Bounds: Exact Formula (b-a)/2^n
content: bisectStep_width proves by pure ring arithmetic (no induction needed) that each step exactly halves the width. bisect_width then proves by induction that after n steps the width is exactly (p.2 - p.1)/2^n. The inductive step rewrites using bisectStep_width and the IH, then closes by ring. This clean exact formula (rather than an inequality) is what enables the precise δ-bound in the main theorem.
mathContext: After $n$ bisection steps: $(\text{bisect}(f,n,p))_2 - (\text{bisect}(f,n,p))_1 = (p_2 - p_1) / 2^n$. Each step: width $\mapsto$ width$/2$. Total shrinkage: factor $1/2^n$.

title: Sign Invariant: f(left) ≤ 0 ≤ f(right) Preserved
content: bisectStep_sign proves that each bisection step preserves the sign invariant f(left) ≤ 0 ≤ f(right). The proof splits on whether f(mid) ≤ 0: if yes, the new left is mid and new right is the old right (f(mid) ≤ 0 ✓, f(right) ≥ 0 ✓); if no, i.e., f(mid) > 0, the new right is mid and new left is the old left (f(left) ≤ 0 ✓, f(mid) > 0 means f(new right) > 0 ✓). The bisect_sign induction is then trivial.
mathContext: Invariant: $f(l_n) \leq 0 \leq f(r_n)$ for all $n$. By the classical IVT, there must be a zero in $[l_n, r_n]$ at every stage. The constructive content makes the nested interval sequence explicit.

title: Interval Containment: bisect(f,n,(a,b)) ⊆ [a,b]
content: bisect_left_mono and bisect_right_mono prove the left endpoint is non-decreasing and the right endpoint is non-increasing (both by induction + split_ifs). Together they give bisect_contained: the n-th bisection interval is contained in the original [a,b]. bisectMid_mem then shows the midpoint lies in [a,b], using containment + ordering (ordering ensures left ≤ right, so mid = (left+right)/2 ∈ [left, right] ⊆ [a,b]).
mathContext: $a \leq l_n \leq r_n \leq b$ for all $n$. Combined with $l_n \leq r_n$: the midpoint $(l_n + r_n)/2 \in [l_n, r_n] \subseteq [a,b]$.

title: Main Theorem: Approximate IVT via Bisection
content: approx_ivt is the main result: for continuous f on [a,b] with f(a) ≤ 0 ≤ f(b), for any ε > 0 there exists x ∈ [a,b] with |f(x)| < ε. The proof extracts δ from uniform continuity (compactness of [a,b] gives uniform continuity via isCompact_Icc), chooses n via the Archimedean property (exists_pow_lt_of_lt_one: (1/2)^n < δ/(b-a)), then uses the midpoint of the n-th bisection interval. The midpoint is within (b-a)/2^(n+1) of both endpoints, hence within δ of both, so uniform continuity gives |f(x) - f(left)| < ε and |f(x) - f(right)| < ε. The sign invariant forces |f(x)| < ε.
mathContext: Given $\varepsilon > 0$: find $\delta$ (uniform continuity of $f$ on $[a,b]$), then $n$ with $(b-a)/2^n < \delta$. Midpoint $x = (l_n+r_n)/2$ satisfies $|x - l_n| = |x - r_n| = (r_n-l_n)/2 < \delta$. By UC: $|f(x)-f(l_n)| < \varepsilon$ and $|f(x)-f(r_n)| < \varepsilon$. Sign invariant $f(l_n) \leq 0 \leq f(r_n)$ then forces $|f(x)| < \varepsilon$.

title: Uniqueness of Zero via Strict Monotonicity
content: monotone_ivt_unique proves that for strictly monotone f on [a,b] with f(a) < 0 < f(b), the zero is unique (∃! x ∈ [a,b], f(x) = 0). Existence uses Mathlib's intermediate_value_Icc directly; uniqueness by contradiction: if x ≠ y are both zeros, then x < y or y < x, and in either case strict monotonicity gives f(x) < f(y) = 0 or f(y) < f(x) = 0, a contradiction. This recovers the full exact IVT for monotone functions.
mathContext: If $f$ is strictly monotone on $[a,b]$ with $f(a) < 0 < f(b)$, then $\exists! x \in [a,b], f(x) = 0$. Uniqueness: if $f(x) = f(y) = 0$ and $x < y$, then $f(x) < f(y)$ by $\text{StrictMonoOn}$ — contradiction.

title: Summary: Three Constructive Guarantees
content: constructive_ivt_summary packages three guarantees: (1) approximate roots ∀ ε > 0, ∃ x ∈ [a,b], |f(x)| < ε; (2) midpoint containment ∀ n, bisectMid ∈ [a,b]; (3) width → 0: ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, width < ε. The third requires an Archimedean argument and implies the bisection midpoints form a Cauchy sequence. By completeness of ℝ, they converge to a limit, which is an exact zero by (1). This is how the constructive approximate IVT recovers the classical existence statement.
mathContext: The three guarantees together imply: the bisection midpoints form a Cauchy sequence $(x_n) \subset [a,b]$ with $|f(x_n)| < 1/n$. By completeness of $\mathbb{R}$: $x_n \to x^*$, and by continuity $f(x^*) = 0$.
